newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond new issue market sizzles.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond new issue market sizzles.

text.p: Corporate bond new issue activity continues to sizzle as underwriters prepare to launch several new debt offerings, syndicate sources said.
"I think you'll see a lot of activity today," said one high-grade syndicate source. "There's a positive tone in the market...Treasuries have been fairly stable."
"I'd watch the 10-year sector...it's probably going to experience a couple of wide swings today in light of the new 10-year corporate supply that's coming," the source added.
Among issuers of 10-year paper today, Merrill Lynch & Co is expected to issue $350 million in Aa3/AA-minus rated 10-year debt for themselves, sources said.
Price talk on the issue is in the 59 basis points over Treasuries arena.
Dealers said the issue is already being sought after on the Street and may have to be upped in size to meet investor demand.
"Merrill's issue is very aggressively bid for on the Street," one syndicate source said.
Among other issuers expected to tap the market are US West Capital Funding Inc, a unit of US West, with a $2.0 billion four-part debt offering via Merrill Lynch, sources said.
The A2/BBB-plus rated deal is expected to consist of five, 10, 30 and 40-year maturities, they added.
Also, Tosco Corp is expected to tap the market midweek with a $600 million three-part debt offering via Morgan Stanley & Co, sources said.
The Tosco deal is expected consist of $200 million in 10-year debt, $300 million in 30-year debt and $100 million in 50-year debt, sources added.
Lehman Brothers Inc is expected to tap the market with $200 million in 10-year debt, syndicate source said. Price talk on the deal is seen between 92 and 95 basis points over Treasuries.
Lehman Brothers is also expected to underwrite a $250 million two-part Baa3/BBB rated debt offering for Polaroid Corp this week, syndicate sources added.
The offering is expected to consist of $100 million in five-year debt and $150 in ten-year debt, sources added.
Baxter International may also tap the market this week but some players said the deal may come as next week's business.

Baxter's deal is expected to consist of $450 million in A3/A rated two-part debt via Goldman Sachs & Co. The first tranche is expected to consist of $250 million in 10-year debt and the second tranche of $200 million in 30-year debt, sources said.
Orion Capital Corp and Markel Corp are currently structuring their own trust preferred deals and are expected to come to market this week as well, syndicate sources said.
TCI Communications Inc is expected to issue $500 million in trust preferred securities one day next week via Lehman Brothers.

Turning to the high-yield sector, Tenet HealthCare is getting set to bring a two-part debt offering consisting of $800 million in notes due 2005 and $500 million in notes due 2007, market sources said.
The deal is expected to be underwritten by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
Also, Multicanal SA, an Argentinian cable company, is expected to sell $250 million in junk bonds via a 144A private debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
Orion Network Systems is expected to bring a two-part deal consisting of $222 million in senior notes due 2007 and $100 million in senior discount notes via Morgan Stanley.

Among new zero coupon bond deals, Optelcom is expected to issue $150 million in zeros, General Wireless is preparing a $220 million deal and UIH Australia/Pacific Inc is expected to issue a $150 million zero coupon issue, dealers said.
Currently, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is up 5/32 at 96-14/32 to yield 6.78 percent.

Merrill Lynch is expected to underwrite a $300 million two-part deal for Reliance Industries, sources said. The deal is expected to consist of $200 million in 30-year bonds with a put option in the tenth year, and $100 million of noncallable 100-year bonds.
Among trust preferred deals Aon Corp is expected to bring its $700 million 30-year trust preferred issue via Morgan Stanley & Co as early as this week, sources said.
BankAmerica Corp is also expected to tap the market with $450 million in A1/A-minus rated trust preferred securities due 2026.
((--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675))
